title: Pulmonary Diagnostics I Module Review Quiz

questions.text: What syringe is used to calibrate the PFT machine daily?
Before spirometry or post-bronchodilator testing, what medication class should the patient withhold when ordered?
Which patient information is used to calculate predicted spirometry values?

answers.text: Age, height or arm span, sex, and race
Pulse, respiratory rate, temperature, and blood pressure
Medication list, allergies, oxygen device, and sleep position

questions.text: How many spirometry efforts should be obtained that meet ATS acceptability and reproducibility criteria?
What minimum exhalation times are highlighted for adults/patients 10 years or older and children 10 years or younger?

answers.text: 3 seconds for adults and 6 seconds for children
6 seconds for adults and 3 seconds for children
8 seconds for adults and 12 seconds for children
15 seconds for adults and 20 seconds for children

questions.text: How many attempts are allowed to obtain three good spirometry tests?
What does a PFT value between LLN and ULN mean?
Which FVC percent predicted result is normal according to the review?
What spirometry value is the best value to grade airway obstruction severity?
An FEV1/FVC ratio greater than 100% or greater than ULN suggests which pattern?
An FEV1/FVC ratio less than 70% suggests which pattern?
FEF25%-75% evaluates flow in which airways?

answers.text: Only the upper airway during sleep

questions.text: What does a pre/post bronchodilator study determine?

answers.text: Thoracic gas volume by Boyle's law

questions.text: How many MDI puffs are used in the ATS post-bronchodilator source protocol?
Which formula calculates post-bronchodilator percent change?
What increase indicates significant airway reversibility after bronchodilator?

answers.text: FEV1 or FVC increase greater than 12% and 200 mL

questions.text: How is MVV performed according to the review?
Which lung volume method is also called VTG, body plethysmography, or body box?
Body plethysmography is based on which law?
What panting frequency is used during body box testing?
Which TLC result is graded as mild restriction?

answers.text: TLC less than LLN but at least 70% predicted
TLC less than 70% but at least 60% predicted
FRC and TLC greater than ULN

questions.text: FRC greater than ULN with TLC within normal limits represents what pattern?
FRC and TLC both greater than ULN represent what pattern?
Nitrogen washout uses what oxygen concentration?
Nitrogen washout lasts up to how long, or until exhaled N2 is below what value?

answers.text: 4 minutes or until N2 is below 10%
7 minutes or until N2 is below 1%
15 minutes or until N2 is below 5%
20-30 minutes or until N2 is below 15%

questions.text: What absorber is required during helium dilution?
Before DLCO testing, why should the patient avoid smoking the day of the test?

answers.text: To reduce CO levels in the blood
To reduce N2 levels in the spirometer

questions.text: What DLCO maneuver sequence is highlighted?

answers.text: Inhale to TLC, exhale to RV, then pant 30-60 bpm
Exhale to RV, inhale rapidly to TLC, hold 8-12 seconds
Exercise for 6-8 minutes, then repeat spirometry
Take five 15-minute naps separated by 2-hour breaks

questions.text: What is the minimum number of DLCO tests and the wait time between trials?

answers.text: Two tests with at least 4 minutes between trials
Three tests with 30 seconds between trials
Eight tests with 15 minutes between trials

questions.text: During methacholine challenge, spirometry is repeated looking for a significant decrease in which value?
What baseline FEV1 is required to start methacholine challenge?
What post-diluent NaCl response makes the methacholine test positive and terminated before methacholine dosing?

answers.text: FEV1 drops 10% or greater from baseline

questions.text: What FEV1 response after methacholine dose is considered a positive methacholine challenge?

answers.text: Sustained FVC increase of 200 mL only

questions.text: For EIA/EIB testing, what should the patient avoid before the test?

answers.text: Heavy exercise for at least 4 hours

questions.text: What exercise target is used during EIA/EIB testing?
What sustained FEV1 decrease is considered a positive EIA/EIB test?
CPX/CPET assesses which three systems during exercise?

answers.text: Ventilation, gas exchange, and cardiovascular function
Sleep latency, REM entry, and alertness

questions.text: Which room-air values are listed as CPX contraindications?

answers.text: PaO2 less than 40 mmHg or PaCO2 greater than 70 mmHg
PaO2 greater than 80 mmHg or PaCO2 less than 35 mmHg
SpO2 greater than 93% and HR less than 60
AHI less than 5 and FEV1 greater than 80%

questions.text: What gases do CPX gas analyzers measure in exhaled gas?
Which pair accounts for the majority of deaths associated with bronchoscopy?
Which is an absolute contraindication to bronchoscopy?
Which bronchoscopy route is most common, and what is needed for the mouth route?

answers.text: Transnasal is most common; transoral requires a bite block
Transoral is most common; transnasal requires a body box
Transnasal is most common; transoral requires soda lime
Transoral is most common; transnasal requires Saccomanno solution

questions.text: What does PSG definitively diagnose in the review sheet?
What pattern defines obstructive sleep apnea?

answers.text: Respiratory effort but no airflow due to upper airway obstruction
CNS fails to signal respiratory effort
No respiratory effort and normal airflow
Five naps with REM entry twice

questions.text: What pattern defines central sleep apnea?

answers.text: CNS fails to signal respiratory effort
Effort but no airflow from upper airway obstruction
FRC and TLC are both above ULN

questions.text: What does actigraphy monitor?

answers.text: Rest/activity cycles by movement of a limb
CO uptake during a breath hold
Thoracic gas volume by shutter panting

questions.text: How is the MSLT structured?

answers.text: Four sleep trials with 2-hour breaks while trying to stay awake
Exercise at 80-90% max HR for 6-8 minutes
Panting at 30-60 bpm in a closed body box

questions.text: What does the MWT measure?

answers.text: How alert a patient is during the day
How much CO crosses the alveolar membrane
How much N2 washes out of the lungs
How much FEV1 improves after bronchodilator

questions.text: Which AHI value is rated severe sleep apnea?
What is CPAP first-line therapy for, and what is key for successful PAP treatment?
